A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Deep Value Benchmark study, including appendices A–N and the checklist. Some appendix prompts overflow the page in v3, but their complete wording is recoverable from the PDF text, permitting reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of nine LLMs, three human validation studies, and supplementary experiments, including an overall DVGR of 0.30.

after.justification: v3 retains these original model evaluations, human validation results, and supplementary experiments.

M1.justification: The confound-then-deconfound design, benchmark generation algorithm, prompting procedures, and DVGR calculation are unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the generation prompt are relocated without changes to their content.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight domains, eleven deep values, twenty shallow preferences, benchmark scenarios, and human and LLM validation tasks. No coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Section 5 retains the same nine evaluated LLMs. Table 1 retains the same baseline, chain-of-thought, and explicit-instruction comparisons for those models.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated in-context example counts from {5, 20, 40} to {4, 20, 40} in two places. This aligns the setup with the four-example results and Appendix H already present in v1; it does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The preference-selection robustness checks, adjusted-DVGR analysis, model similarity analysis, value-rating investigation, prompting experiments, and LLM validations are all retained without substantive revision.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same confidence intervals, statistical tests, mixed-effects analyses, clustered standard errors, power calculations, and ten-iteration value-rating procedure.

E6.justification: All reported results match, including overall DVGR of 0.30, the model and prompting results in Tables 1 and 7, human validation outcomes, and appendix analyses. Section 6 already reports the four-example condition in v1, so the setup correction adds no new result.

T1.justification: The DVGR definition, benchmark tuple definitions, preference-ranking formulas, and statistical model specifications are unchanged. Neither version adds formal theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The benchmark and dataset contributions and principal claims remain unchanged: models favor shallow preferences, scaling does not reliably help, and explicit instructions provide limited improvement.

C2.justification: Section 7 and the appendices retain the same interpretations and limitations, including artificial perfect confounding, ambiguity about value-aligned choices, inference-only evaluation, and restricted model and value coverage.

D1.justification: Correcting the smallest demonstration count to four makes the implementation description consistent with Section 6 and Appendix H, improving reproducibility documentation. Prompt wording, software and compute details, and dataset access information are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Correcting 'W.B. Ross' to 'W.D. Ross' in Section 3.1 does not change the referenced work or its role.

P1.justification: Limited editorial changes expand 'Sai Avula' to 'Saipranav Avula', correct Ross's initials, and change 'users' to 'a user' in Figure 1. The narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 5 and Algorithm 1 exchange order, and Figure 6 moves to the preceding page with associated reflow. Removed line wrapping makes Figure 5 and the Appendix K prompt boxes overflow the right page edge, clipping visible instructions.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves the five-versus-four demonstration inconsistency and corrects names, but introduces visibly clipped prompt instructions in Figure 5 and rating questions in Appendix K. Although their wording remains extractable, these technical details become harder to read and use. With scientific evidence unchanged, this usability loss outweighs the limited corrections.
